statements.venue: Letter from 17 senators to President Trump
statements.quote: China to develop a formal agreement that would slow down, and potentially enact a mutual pause in, frontier AI development to prevent cyberattacks, the development of biological weapons, and other dangerous activities that threaten the lives of the American people and humanity writ large
statements.context: The senators urged the President to negotiate AI guardrails with Xi Jinping at the summit planned for 24 September 2026.
statements.source_label: Sen. Van Hollen press release (full letter text)
statements.reason: The letter she signed says frontier AI development could enable activities that threaten humanity, which is level A under ruling 1; these are the letter's words, not her individual words.

statements.venue: Letter from 17 senators to President Trump
statements.quote: While advanced AI may be new, engagement between two superpowers over a technology that poses an existential threat is not.
statements.context: The letter compares a US-China AI agreement to Cold War nuclear arms control agreements.
statements.source_label: Sen. Van Hollen press release (full letter text)
statements.reason: The letter she signed calls AI a technology that poses an existential threat.

statements.source_label: Senate Commerce Committee (Democrats) press release with speech text
statements.reason: In her own words she names biological weapons and autonomous cyberattacks as real dangers from advanced AI, without extinction framing.

statements.source_label: Senate Commerce Committee (Democrats) press release with speech text
statements.reason: She says concern about superintelligence is well founded but does not name a catastrophic consequence in this passage.

slowdown.note: She signed the 23 September 2026 letter calling for a formal agreement with China that "would slow down" frontier AI development to prevent dangers including biological weapons. This is a signed letter; I found no statement in her own words calling for a slowdown, and her own framework asks for standards, testing and audits before release rather than slower development.
sources: Sen. Van Hollen press release, 23 Sep 2026

pause.note: The letter she signed asks for an agreement with China that would "potentially enact a mutual pause" in frontier AI development; that is a pause conditional on China joining, and only a possible one. Signed letter, not her own words.
sources: Sen. Van Hollen press release, 23 Sep 2026

intl.note: She signed the letter urging a formal US-China agreement to slow, and possibly mutually pause, frontier AI development. Separately, her own framework proposes a US-China crisis channel "like the Soviet era red phone", which is about incident communication rather than pacing.
sources: Sen. Van Hollen press release, 23 Sep 2026

rsi.note: Her framework asks for heightened oversight of systems capable of self-improvement, stress tests that systems halt self-modification that bypasses safety controls, and reporting of unsafe recursive self-improvement. That is regulation, not a ban, and I found no statement for or against a ban.

record: Signed the letter from 17 Senate Democrats, led by Sen. Van Hollen, urging President Trump to negotiate a formal AI agreement with China, including a slowdown and possible mutual pause in frontier AI development.
Gave a Senate floor speech on AI risks, including swarms of AI agents, calling for federal standards and independent testing of frontier models.

Published a six-principle governance framework for frontier AI: federal standards for catastrophic risks, continuous testing, independent audits before release, incident reporting, and a US-China crisis channel.
At a Commerce Committee hearing, said federal agencies and national laboratories must lead testing of frontier AI models, citing biological weapons and cyberattack risks.

Co-led, with Sen. Blackburn, the amendment that removed a ten-year moratorium on state AI regulation from the budget reconciliation bill by a 99-1 vote (about state regulation, not a pause in AI development). Seen in search results only; page not opened.
Senate Commerce Committee (Democrats) press release, July 2025
grade_reason: The A rests only on the 23 September 2026 letter she co-signed, which says frontier AI could enable activities that threaten "humanity writ large" and calls AI "a technology that poses an existential threat". Her own individual words reach level B (biological weapons, loss of human control named as catastrophic risks), so a reviewer who discounts co-signed letters should use B.
notes: Seven web searches ran; none was refused. All four quoted pages were downloaded and each quote was checked by exact string match against the page text. The search tool's page reader could not open the GeekWire article on the floor speech (error 403), so it was not used. Left out because they are not her own words: in the floor speech she read out warnings by Bill Gates ("we could lose control") and Dario Amodei (a swarm "could have caused catastrophic damage") and then said "We know that these threats are real"; a reviewer may wish to count these as endorsed relayed warnings at level B. The framework quotes are the published wording of her framework, not speech. Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act: search results name only Sen. Sanders as Senate sponsor (with Rep. Casar); no source shows Cantwell as a co-sponsor, and I did not check congress.gov. Not verified at source (search results only): a Semafor report of 10 Sep 2026 saying she wants a stricter version of a bipartisan AI safety bill; a report that she and Sen. Rounds asked the administration to expand federal AI safety testing (about 14 Oct 2026); her reintroduction of the Future of AI Innovation Act in 2026; and the 2025 state-moratorium item in the record list. The floor speech date (15 Sep 2026) is the date shown on the press release.
